claims.text_en: Merge semantics resolved: the unit pairs MRT Phetchaburi (BL21, Blue Line, under the junction of Asok and New Phetchaburi Road) with ARL Makkasan (opened 23 August 2010; every ARL station except Suvarnabhumi and Ratchaprarop sits above an Eastern Line station), which Wikipedia connects via 'a covered-elevated footpath' with fares and ticket systems 'not integrated'. OSM nodes are ~312 m apart - inside the <=450 m merge rule - and an area portal treats them as a single interchange (codes BL21 / A6). A third rail element, the SRT Eastern Line's Asok Halt at ground level, sits adjacent (OSM halt node ~200 m from the MRT node).

claims.text_en: The app's '3 piers' are identified and none is named Makkasan: on the Khlong Saen Saep NIDA Line they are Asoke-Petchaburi (~157 m from the MRT node - Wikipedia: 'near Phetchaburi MRT station and the old site of the Japanese embassy'), Prasanmit (~321 m, at Srinakharinwirot University's Prasarn Mit campus) and Nana Chard (~474 m, Sukhumvit Soi 15). The boat service has run since 1 October 1990 over an 18 km route, operating 05:30-20:30 weekdays and to 19:00 weekends at 8-22 THB with ~60,000 daily passengers, running parallel to Phetchaburi Road.

claims.text_en: The SRT railway-community relocation to Bueng Makkasan is real and dated: on 29 September 2024 the 'ชุมชน ชมฟ.ริมบึงมักกะสัน' community - railway-track households displaced by the Don Mueang-Suvarnabhumi-U-Tapao high-speed rail, which reuses the ARL corridor with ARL Makkasan as its EEC gateway - unveiled its sign on ~7 rai leased from the SRT beside Santiphap Park in Ratchathewi. Phase 1 covers 169 households of the 644 affected across five communities stretching along the Rama VI to Phaya Thai corridor (บุญร่มไทร 129, แดงบุหงา 151, หลัง รพ.เดชา 182, หมอเหล็ง 124, RCA 58); a cabinet programme of 14 March 2023 funds housing for 27,084 rail-affected households nationwide (2023-2027), and a separate NHA 315-unit block at Bueng Makkasan was reported in 2022 with construction from 2024. The relocation site computes to ~2.3 km from the MRT Phetchaburi node - outside this unit - though the cleared corridor edges approach it.

claims.text_en: Counter-view to nightlife 9 with only 11 venues: independent guides flatly deny the area is a nightlife district - 'Pratunam remains active after dark, but it is not one of Bangkok's strongest nightlife districts... better for casual food, shopping, massage... than cocktail-bar hopping or clubbing' and 'not a neighborhood for serious bar culture'. The 9 most plausibly aggregates hotel-bar venues along New Phetchaburi Road (e.g. a Novotel rooftop bar) and the Palladium/Pratunam night-market belt at the Ratchaprarop x Phetchaburi corner (~1.2 km west) - a buffer effect rather than in-unit club density.

Transport 9 = merged MRT+ARL with airport access and three canal piers; DE 8 = MetroMall + market + Pratunam belt; rent 6 = mid-band medians slightly above the app's 21,000.
Nightlife 9 vs 11 venues: guides deny nightlife-district status; the 9 is likely buffer + hotel-bar aggregation.
Canal boats 05:30-20:30 weekdays shape the morning; office peaks; Pratunam's evening market belt to the west.

Strong fit: Asok/Rama 9 office workers and frequent flyers wanting lower rents than Asok; poor fit: nightlife-first and park-seeking renters.

Outside the score: nightlife-9 buffer artifact risk, unnamed park polygon, anchor offset toward Makkasan, and the displacement story invisible to amenity counts.

preview.text_en: The quietest core unit in the dataset hides a triple rail identity: MRT Phetchaburi and ARL Makkasan 312 m apart under a covered walkway, an 'Asok' SRT halt between them, three Khlong Saen Saep piers within 500 m - and a railway corridor being cleared for the three-airport high-speed line.

guide_lead.text_en: Phetchaburi/Makkasan is the app's connector unit: MRT Blue Line BL21 under the Asok-New Phetchaburi junction, the Airport Rail Link's Makkasan station 312 m away via a covered footpath (fares not integrated), and an SRT halt called Asok at ground level - three names, one block. The canal adds three piers (Asoke-Petchaburi, Prasanmit, Nana Chard) and a 05:30-20:30 boat commute. Rents run mid-band (800 m 1-BR medians 25-29.5k; the app's 21,000 fits older Makkasan-Road stock). What the score glosses: nightlife 9 rests on hotel bars and the Pratunam night-market belt - guides call this area no nightlife district at all - the 0.5 ha park is unidentified, and the railway corridor along the unit's edge is being progressively cleared, with 644 households affected and the first 169 rehoused beside Santiphap Park in September 2024.

strengths.text_en: Three-rail access plus a boat: merged MRT-ARL interchange with airport line service and three canal piers inside ~500 m - a genuinely multi-modal transport set for the price band.
Rents still sit below the Asok towers next door: 800 m medians of 25-29.5k THB against the app's 21,000 for older stock.

tradeoffs.text_en: Nightlife 9 is the least defensible rating in this batch: with 11 mapped venues, the number borrows from hotel bars and the Pratunam belt that guides explicitly do not consider a nightlife district.
The street layer is rough: narrow pavements on Asok-Din Daeng, single-in/out sois that back up at peak, and an unresolved 0.5 ha park.

day_night.text_en: Canal boats and office peaks own the morning (first boats 05:30); the block quiets after work, leaving evenings to the Pratunam night-market belt one district west.

within_area_variation.text_en: The station-and-walkway block is transit-busy; eastward toward the piers the canal side is quieter, and the railway-corridor edge carries the clearance works and pending land plans.

conditional_fit.text_en: Strong fit: Asok/Rama 9 office workers and frequent flyers who want multi-modal access at rents below the neighbouring Asok towers.
Poor fit: nightlife-led renters and green-space seekers - both headline ratings trace to buffers, not to this block's own amenities.
